Introduction to ChromaDB
Simple, local, and efficient vector database for AI applications
Introduction
The explosion in the use of language models has brought a new type of challenge for data engineering: how to store, search, and relate information semantically, not just by text equality.
Keyword search is useful. But asking “tell me about expired contracts” and getting relevant documents requires something else: vector representation.
This is exactly where ChromaDB comes in: a lightweight, easy-to-use vector database perfect for AI projects that need:
•
semantic search
•
recommendation systems
•
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
•
agent memory
•
semantic text indexing
•
context retrieval for LLMs
In this article, you’ll learn:
What ChromaDB is ✅How it works ✅When to use it ✅A complete hands-on lab ✅And how to integrate it into real applications
What is ChromaDB
ChromaDB is a vector database designed to store texts, metadata, and their embedding vectors, allowing you to perform searches by semantic similarity, not string equality.
While traditional databases think in terms of:
WHERE nome = 'Ana'
ChromaDB thinks in terms of:
“Bring me texts most similar to this idea.”
Internally, it transforms texts into numerical vectors and measures the distance between them using similarity algorithms - like cosine similarity.
In other words: it’s not a database for storing files. It’s a database for storing meaning.
When to use ChromaDB
Use ChromaDB when your system needs:
•
Find similar texts
•
Maintain memory for AI agents
•
Provide context to language models
•
Index documents by meaning
•
Create intelligent FAQs
•
Implement document-based chat
•
Build RAG systems
It’s not a replacement for PostgreSQL. It’s not a competitor to MongoDB. It solves a different type of problem.
How it works
The typical flow is:
Raw text → Embedding → Vector → ChromaDB → Semantic search
Instead of searching for words, you search for similar vectors.
Hands-on lab: ChromaDB from scratch
Objective
We’ll create a semantic document base and search it by meaning.
Prerequisites
Create a virtualenv:
python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate
Install:
pip install chromadb sentence-transformers
Creating a vector collection
Create the file chroma_lab.py:
import chromadb from chromadb.utils import embedding_functions # Local embedding function (no API) embedding_function = embedding_functions.SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction( model_name="all-MiniLM-L6-v2" ) client = chromadb.Client() colecao = client.get_or_create_collection( name="base_conhecimento", embedding_function=embedding_function ) print("Collection created.") #Inserting documents #Now let's create semantic data: docs = [ "The contract expired in January and needs to be renewed.", "The financial system had a payment failure.", "The security policy was updated in March.", "The client requested service cancellation.", "The invoice was paid late." ] colecao.add( documents=docs, ids=[str(i) for i in range(len(docs))] ) print("Documents indexed.")
Run:
python chroma_lab.py
Querying by meaning
Now add the search:
resultado = colecao.query( query_texts=["expired documents"], n_results=3 ) print("Semantic results:") for doc in resultado["documents"][0]: print("-", doc)
Run again:
python chroma_lab.py
Typical result:
Notice: No exact word search. It’s pure meaning.
Complete script
import chromadb from chromadb.utils import embedding_functions from chromadb.config import Settings # ================================ # 1. ChromaDB Client with persistence # ================================ client = chromadb.Client( Settings( persist_directory="./chroma_data", anonymized_telemetry=False ) ) # ================================ # 2. Local embedding function # ================================ embedding_function = embedding_functions.SentenceTransformerEmbeddingFunction( model_name="all-MiniLM-L6-v2" ) # ================================ # 3. Create or open collection # ================================ colecao = client.get_or_create_collection( name="base_conhecimento", embedding_function=embedding_function ) print("Collection created/opened.") # ================================ # 4. Semantic documents # ================================ docs = [ "The contract expired in January and needs to be renewed.", "The financial system had a payment failure.", "The security policy was updated in March.", "The client requested service cancellation.", "The invoice was paid late." ] ids = [f"doc-{i}" for i in range(len(docs))] # Remove if they already exist to avoid duplication try: colecao.delete(ids=ids) except Exception: pass # ================================ # 5. Inserting the documents # ================================ colecao.add( documents=docs, ids=ids ) print("Documents indexed.") # ================================ # 6. Semantic query # ================================ consulta = "expired documents" resultado = colecao.query( query_texts=[consulta], n_results=3 ) print(" Semantic results for:", consulta) for doc in resultado["documents"][0]: print("-", doc)
Using ChromaDB with real applications
Typical scenarios:
Chat with documents
You load PDFs, index texts, and provide context to the LLM.
Agents with memory
Each interaction becomes an embedding and gets stored.
Intelligent FAQ
You search for similar questions and return answers.
Recommendation
You recommend based on behavior similarity.
ChromaDB vs other vector databases
ChromaDB wins in simplicity and speed for real projects.
ChromaDB is the best choice for:
•
labs
•
POCs
•
local agents
•
embedded RAG
•
small and medium applications
Common mistakes
❌ Trying to use it as a relational database ❌ Recreating the client with different settings ❌ Not persisting data ❌ Mixing types without metadata ❌ Indexing texts without prior cleaning
Conclusion
ChromaDB doesn’t store texts. It stores meanings.
In a scenario where:
•
context matters
•
memory is essential
•
similarity beats syntax
•
AI depends on retrieved knowledge
ChromaDB stops being just another tool - and becomes a fundamental part of the AI infrastructure.
If you work with:
•
autonomous agents
•
corporate chatbots
•
RAG
•
semantic systems
ChromaDB is the best starting point.
